conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-sym:
Conjecture The q-difference kernel R is the jet-prolongation symbol, carried by the binding q-lift module. The q-difference kernel R(q,x) of the binding generating function (The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence) is the symbol of the jet-prolongation operator J^{n}E\to J^{n+1}E of the Seiberg--Witten connection (Abelianisation of the MI integral on exceptional divisors).

For jet spaces, their prolongations and the Cartan distribution, see [pugliese2023, §1.1--1.2]. For linear q-difference modules, fundamental solution matrices at 0 and \infty, the q-Borel and q-Laplace transforms and the resulting connection matrices, see [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §2.2--2.3].

Its carrier is the rank-2 q-difference module \mathcal{K} of the binding q-lift recurrence

[m+2]_q\,b_{m+2} \;=\; b_{m+1} + b_m ,

equivalently, writing x=q^{m} and \sigma:x\mapsto qx, the module of

L_{\mathcal{K}} \;=\; (q^{2}x-1)\,\sigma^{2}\;-\;(q-1)\,\sigma\;-\;(q-1).

At x=\infty the Newton polygon of L_{\mathcal{K}} has the single slope \tfrac12 with multiplicity 2: \mathcal{K} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12.

Scope note. This conjecture previously continued "— equivalently, the monodromy/Stokes data of the prolonged SW connection at the branch-point poles of \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}", identifying \mathcal{K} with the Stokes carrier of the resurgent colored-Jones series of [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]. That equivalence is false as an identification of q-difference modules, and the clause has been removed. The Stokes carrier is the module \mathcal{G} of y_{m+2}-(2-q^{m+1})\,y_{m+1}+y_m=0, whose Newton polygon at x=\infty has the two slopes \{-1,+1\}; \mathcal{K}'s is \{\tfrac12,\tfrac12\}. Since the Newton polygon is a module invariant and its slope multiset is preserved by every gauge transformation ([rsz2013] Thm 2.2.1(i), Thm 2.2.4), no isomorphism of q-difference modules \mathcal{K}\cong\mathcal{G} exists.

Two consequences follow:

  1. R is structurally fixed, not fitted. The prolongation operator is a single fibre-level object; its symbol is read off the connection, not tuned to reproduce the terms. This is forced by the precision-floor obstruction (the c_k information bound makes term data unable to fix R beyond low order), and it is the same fibre-level / root-of-unity singularity structure that governs the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder.
  2. It closes the binding program. Given R, the recurrence of The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence determines every body term from the deuteron base case (fixing the \rho\cdot A growth law), which is precisely the per-term mass identity. Feeding it into Binding closure, conditional on the per-term mass identity discharges its one conditional input, promoting Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration: B(K)=\sum_n m_e\,a_D^{(n)} from conditional to unconditional.

This conjecture is therefore the single remaining input to the binding closure: the residue form, the body-order = jet-degree coincidence, and the recurrence machinery are all proved; only the identification of R with the prolongation symbol remains. It is stated here as a precise, falsifiable structural claim — to be derived from the prolonged connection's local monodromy, not fitted numerically.

Scope of Consequence 2 — \mathcal{K} is irreducible, so the rank-1 claim is wrong by exactly one initial condition. The pure-isoclinic slope-\tfrac12 statement above has a consequence the conjecture did not draw. A rank-1 q-difference module over \mathbb{Q}(q)(x) has integer slope, and Newton slopes are additive on sub- and quotient modules — the same invariant, and the same citation ([rsz2013] Thm 2.2.1(i), Thm 2.2.4), that the scope note above uses to separate \mathcal{K} from \mathcal{G}. Since \{\tfrac12,\tfrac12\} contains no integer, \mathcal{K} has no rank-1 sub- or quotient module: it is irreducible. Equivalently, and provable without any module theory, the associated q-Riccati (q^2x-1)a(qx)a(x) - (q-1)a(x) - (q-1) = 0 has no solution in K(x), because the three terms of its cleared form have degrees 1+2p, p+u, 2u and the odd/even parity of the outer two forces the maximum to be attained exactly once. This is corroborated by the van der Put--Reversat classification [vanderput-reversat2007, vanderput2006] of pure modules of non-integral slope d/r — the normal form E(r,d,b) in Bugeaud's notation [bugeaud2011] — which is irreducible when the rank equals r; here r = 2 = \mathrm{rank}\mathcal{K}.

Two revisions follow.

  1. Consequence 1 is unchanged but must be read in rank 2. The prolongation symbol of a rank-2 carrier is a 2\times2 matrix A(q,x) acting on (G,\sigma G), not a scalar R(q,x). The claim that the symbol is structurally fixed rather than fitted is untouched; only its shape changes. This is the natural reading of the Dirac-type \tau-image asserted in The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence, since a Dirac operator is first-order on a two-component object.
  2. Consequence 2 is falsified as stated. "Given R, the recurrence determines every body term from the deuteron base case" is wrong by exactly one initial condition: a rank-2 module needs two. The n=2 deuteron term alone does not close the recursion; the genuine three-body n=3 term is independently required, and is not fixed by the existing anchors.

This narrows rather than refutes the conjecture: the identification of the kernel with the prolongation symbol remains open and remains the single structural input, but it must be sought as a rank-2 symbol, and the closure it would deliver needs a second base case.

Structure of the prolongation operator on the ramified chart, before it is constructed. The classical lift d/dz is excluded (The classical-jet prolongation of \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}} is exact for n \ge 1), and the residue that a period needs vanishes for it locally, at every branch point, because at z = z_c + t^2 the operator d/dz = (1/2t)\,d/dt reads the t^{-2} residue slot from the constant term with multiplier (-2)+2 = 0. That observation generalises exactly. On the coefficient model f:\mathbb{Z}\to R of a local Laurent expansion, every derivative-like operator is a shift operator (S_{k,c}f)(e) = c(e)\,f(e+k) — a pair (shift k, multiplier c), which is its symbol on the punctured t-disk, and symbols compose by adding shifts and multiplying multipliers along the shift. Two exact facts then constrain any single-shift candidate D_q (over a generic commutative ring):

  1. Residue. If D_q annihilates constants, c(-k) = 0 — as every derivative does: d/dz, its q-deformation [e+2]_q in either q-integer convention, the Jackson operator [e+1]_q in the local coordinate, all because [0]_q = 0 — then for shift k \in \{1, 2\} the residue slot is dead at every jet level on a power-series seed such as the colour-cubic branch. No derivative-like prolongation of shift 1 or 2 can produce the binding period. A residue needs a component with c(-k) \neq 0: a genuine zeroth-order term, which in rank 2 is the connection-matrix datum the previous note already places the symbol in.
  2. Parity. An even shift commutes with the covering monodromy t \mapsto -t; an odd shift anti-commutes, so its jet tower's monodromy eigenvalue alternates as (-1)^n. Carrying that alternation needs an odd shift.

So D_q must have an odd shift and a non-derivative component. Both conditions are derived from the local geometry of \Sigma and the two measured target properties, never from the kernel's coefficients — the anti-fit obligation is respected. D_q is not constructed here; the class is narrowed, which is what the scoping audit's walls W1–W2 asked for first.

The sum case does not behave as the single-shift case suggests. For a finite sum \sum_k c_k\sigma^k the residue slot of the n-th jet is a sum over words, and the word (shift 1, then shift 2) reads t^{-2} from t^{-1} and t^{-1} from t^{+1}, never landing on the constant slot where a derivative's multiplier vanishes. So two derivative-like terms of shifts 1 and 2 — classical d/dt + (1/t)\,d/dt, or Jackson [e+1]_q with [e+2]_q — do reach the residue slot: at level n+2 it is c_1(-2)\,c_2(-1) times the t^{1} coefficient of the level-n jet, weight -1 in both cases. The non-derivative clause is therefore a single-shift statement. What restores it for sums is the residual: an operator with even part E and odd part O satisfies \mathrm{mono}(Df) = E(\mathrm{mono}\,f) - O(\mathrm{mono}\,f), and a tower carrying the full (-1)^n alternation is generated by O alone with E annihilating every level — after which the single-shift prune kills the residue again. For derivative-like sums of shifts \le 2 the residue and the residual are mutually exclusive level by level: alternation demanded from a level n_0 on kills the residue from level n_0+2 on and leaves levels 2,\dots,n_0+1 alive. The distinction matters, because the Door-v alternation of the carrier \mathcal{G} cannot hold at every level — while 2-q^{m+1}>0 no solution flips at two consecutive pairs, so at the substrate value the alternation is absent for m \le 5 and persistent only from m \approx 11 on. The conclusion above therefore stands for sums only above that window; at the low body orders a mixed-shift D_q built from derivatives alone remains admissible by the two target properties, and the non-derivative clause is not forced by them there.

The kernel is a recurrence across jet levels, and on that axis it forces the non-derivative clause too. In L_{\mathcal{K}} the variable is x = q^{m} with m the body order, which The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum identifies with the jet degree; so \sigma is the step from one jet level to the next, and L_{\mathcal{K}} is the second-order recurrence that the level-indexed residues r_{n} = (D_{q}^{n}X)_{t^{-2}} of the prolongation tower must satisfy — never D_{q} itself, which is first-order in the level. On a power-series seed r_{0} = 0 for every operator, so the residue tower cannot coincide with a carrier whose first term is nonzero (the involution-number carrier has b_{0} = b_{1} = 1): the recurrence is demanded from a level on, and a level-n_{0} C1 sequence is fixed by its two values at n_{0} and n_{0}+1 — the two base cases of the scope note above. For the admissible two-term operator r_{1} = c_{2}(-2)\,a_{0}, the branch value read through the shift-2 weight at the residue slot; a derivative-like shift-2 term has c_{2}(-2) = 0, so r_{0} = r_{1} = 0 and a C1 residue tower from level 0 is identically zero. For a derivative-only tower the recurrence from level 2 is equivalent to the index-shifted recurrence [m+4]_{q}\,s_{m+2} = s_{m+1} + s_{m} on the tower's t^{1}-coefficients s_{m} = (D_{q}^{m}X)_{t^{1}}, since r_{m+2} = c_{1}(-2)c_{2}(-1)\,s_{m}; each level's constraint reaches one new seed coefficient and none of them reads the branch value a_{0} (for q not a root of unity). On the actual seed — the branch-point expansion of the colour cubic at its simple ramification point — neither the Jackson nor the q-derivative tower, in either q-integer convention and on either sheet, satisfies that recurrence at any tested q: the defect is of order one relative to the residues themselves, not a precision artefact. And with the weights left free, each level introduces at least four new weight values against one constraint, so the recurrence constrains nothing until the weights are supplied by the geometry. Both statements are scope-(a): they concern these two candidates on this seed, and the two-term derivative-only class, respectively. The weights cannot be supplied by a q-connection on the base either: the colour cubic is irreducible over K(z) for every field K of characteristic zero , so no sheet is a rational function of z; each sheet is algebraic, hence D-finite; and a rational rank-3 q-difference system in z \mapsto \lambda z with the sheets as solutions would make a sheet q-holonomic, which together with D-finiteness forces rationality (Bézivin, Ramis; Schäfke–Singer). So a rational q-connection on the z-line with the sheets as flat sections does not exist — scope (b), the cited theorem being the invariant. Localising at the ramification point does not evade this. In the local coordinate t, with z = z_{c} + t^{2}, the sheets are power series algebraic over K(t) and so still D-finite; and they are still not rational, because t^{2} = z - z_{c} makes K(t)/K(z) quadratic while an irreducible cubic has no root of degree at most two. The same theorem therefore excludes the local q-dilation as well, and what survives is an operator whose coefficients are not rational in a coordinate, or one defined on the curve rather than on a coordinate line.

Two earlier readings of the same kernel took \sigma to be a shift in the t-exponent of a single jet — the unit t-shift with x = q^{e}, or the t-shift by two on the double cover. That is the special case in which the level and the exponent lock, r_{n} = c^{n}a_{n-2} for a constant-weight pure shift-1 tower, not the conjecture's reading. What was proved there stands as mathematics about those t-operators: neither can be written as a sum of derivative-like terms, because each carries a zeroth-order term -(q-1) that does not annihilate the constant seed , and neither can carry the (-1)^{m} alternation of the preceding note on a nonzero tower — on the double cover because a monodromy-commuting operator transports the character unchanged, under the unit shift because the even part would have to annihilate both a jet and its odd image, and those two recurrences differ by q^{e+1}(q-1)Y_{e+2}. Read on the correct axis those facts say nothing about D_{q}, and the "\sigma \leftrightarrow t-shift dictionary" they posed as wall W2 is not a question the conjecture asks.

Branch-locus obstruction on the curve — an operator on \Sigma does not evade the exclusion either, when its base map is a dilation. The two preceding exclusions constrain the coefficient field, so an operator living on \Sigma rather than on a coordinate line is not reached by them. It is reached by the branch locus. An automorphism of \Sigma covering the base dilation z \mapsto \lambda z is an isomorphism of coverings up to that base automorphism, so it carries ramification points to ramification points and therefore permutes the six finite branch points — the zeros of the branch sextic D(z) = 16z^{6} + 24z^{5} + 35z^{4} + 50z^{3} + 35z^{2} + 24z + 16, which is squarefree with D(0) = 16 \neq 0. Equal root multisets means D(\lambda z) = c\,D(z), and then two coefficients settle it: the constant term gives 16 = 16c, so c = 1, and the linear term gives 24\lambda = 24, so \lambda = 1 (over a generic characteristic-zero field). Only the identity dilation lifts to \Sigma, for every \lambda and at every q — scope (b), the invariant being the sextic's own coefficients rather than a cited analytic theorem, so this covers the root-of-unity case that the rationality theorem does not. The substrate asks for \lambda = q_{0}^{2} \approx 1.2321, which is excluded both by that identity and by the weaker bound \lambda^{6} = 1 that the product of the roots alone would give. This does not touch a q-difference operator whose base map is not a dilation, nor the fibre monodromy route, which acts on the fibre and is untouched by any statement about maps of the z-line.
rem:ramanujan-equation-connection-prior-:
Remark Prior art: connection formulae for the Ramanujan q-difference equation. Morita works with 0 < |q| < 1 [morita2012, \S 2, p. 7]. The Ramanujan function A_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n^2} (-x)^n / (q;q)_n solves the second-order equation

q x\, u(q^2 x) - u(q x) + u(x) = 0,

whose second solution at the origin is \theta_q(x) times the divergent series {}_2\varphi_0(0, 0; -; q, -x/q) [morita2012, eq. (4), p. 3]. Morita proves two connection formulae between the origin and infinity. With the q-Borel--Laplace transformations of the second kind he writes A_{q^2}(-q^3/x^2) as a \theta-weighted combination of the q-Airy functions \mathrm{Ai}_q(x) and \mathrm{Ai}_q(-x) [morita2012, Theorem, p. 4]. With the transformations of the first kind he expresses the summed divergent series \theta_q(x)\, {}_2f_0(0, 0; -; q, -x/q) through two convergent {}_1\varphi_1 series in 1/x, valid for x \notin [-\lambda; q] [morita2012, Theorem, p. 6].

This is a worked instance of the data the kernel conjecture refers to: a second-order linear q-difference equation with one divergent formal solution, a q-Borel sum of that solution, and an explicit connection matrix between 0 and \infty. The shape is close to the corpus's carrier. In the Ramanujan operator q x\,\sigma^2 - \sigma + 1, as in L_{\mathcal{K}} = (q^2 x - 1)\,\sigma^2 - (q - 1)\,\sigma - (q - 1), the coefficient of \sigma^2 is linear in x and the other two are constant.

The formulae do not transfer as they stand. Morita's q lies inside the unit disc and the corpus's substrate parameter is greater than one, so any comparison first needs q replaced by q^{-1} and the operator rewritten. And L_{\mathcal{K}} is not the Ramanujan operator: its coefficients differ, so its connection matrix has to be computed, not read off. Neither step has been done here.
rem:birkhoff-qdifference-riemann-problem:
Remark Prior art: Birkhoff's connection matrix for q-difference systems, and its hypothesis. Birkhoff studies systems Y(qx) = Q(x)\, Y(x) with |q| > 1 and Q a matrix of polynomials of degree at most \mu [birkhoff1913, \S 18, eq. (54), p. 559]. He restricts to the case in which there are matrix solutions Y_0 at x = 0 and Y_\infty at x = \infty of a prescribed form, built from series analytic at the respective point whose leading coefficients have non-zero determinant; only that case is considered [birkhoff1913, \S 18, p. 561]. The connection matrix P, defined by Y_0(x) = Y_\infty(x)\, P(x), is analytic away from 0 and \infty and satisfies P(qx) = P(x) [birkhoff1913, \S 18, p. 561]. Counting the constants in Y_0, Y_\infty and P that survive the freedom to rescale columns, he finds n^2\mu + 1 characteristic constants, the same number as the invariants of the system, and proves that a system can be constructed with any assigned set of them, up to integer shifts of some exponents [birkhoff1913, \S\S 20--21, pp. 565--566].

This is the original source for the connection matrix between 0 and \infty that the kernel conjecture refers to, and its convention |q| > 1 is the one the corpus uses for the substrate parameter.

It does not cover the corpus's carrier. The module \mathcal{K} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at infinity, so its formal solutions there need the ramified variable x^{1/2} and are not of the form Birkhoff assumes. His existence and counting results therefore do not apply to \mathcal{K} as stated, and citing them does not reopen a route that depends on that hypothesis.
conj:c1-ggm-bar-parity-faces:
Conjecture The binding q-lift module and the resurgent Stokes carrier are bar-parity conjugate faces. Let \mathcal{K} be the rank-2 q-difference module of the binding q-lift recurrence [m+2]_q\,b_{m+2}=b_{m+1}+b_m (The q-difference kernel R is the jet-prolongation symbol, carried by the binding q-lift module), and let \mathcal{G} be the module of

y_{m+2}-(2-q^{m+1})\,y_{m+1}+y_m \;=\; 0,

the Stokes carrier of the resurgent colored-Jones series of [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]. Their Newton polygons at x=\infty are \{\tfrac12,\tfrac12\} and \{-1,+1\}, so \mathcal{K}\not\cong\mathcal{G} as q-difference modules. The conjecture is that they are nevertheless related, and by exactly one twist.

  1. The tensor square has the right graded module. \mathcal{K}^{\otimes 2} is anisoclinic with slopes \{+1,0,-1\}\supset \{+1,-1\}. Doubling the slope \tfrac12 produces the integral slopes the rank-2 comparison could not reach, which is why the Newton-polygon obstruction does not apply to it.
  2. No Stokes obstruction on that piece. On the \{+1,-1\} graded part the unipotent part of the connecting datum is trivial and the connecting matrix is constant, so \mathcal{K}^{\otimes 2} and \mathcal{G} agree as graded modules with their Stokes data.
  3. One residual, and it is a parity. The sole difference is the diagonal \mathbb{Z}/2 character (-1)^{m}: the growing solution of \mathcal{G} alternates in sign, y_{m+1}\sim -q^{m}y_m, while the squares f_+^{2},f_-^{2} built from \mathcal{K} are non-negative and provably cannot. This is the framework's bar-even / bar-odd (\cosh / \sinh) distinction: \mathcal{K} is the bar-even face and \mathcal{G} the bar-odd one.

The obstruction half is proved. No combination \alpha p_n+\beta q_n with \alpha,\beta\ge 0 and p,q\ge 0 can equal a sequence with a single consecutive sign flip: the left side lies in the non-negative cone. Hence the squares cannot reproduce the alternating solution without a sign twist, and the twist is forced rather than fitted.

What is conjectural is the positive half — that after the (-1)^{m} twist the agreement is exact, so that the parity is the whole difference and not merely a difference. Items 1--3 are established at probe level; the exact-coefficient identity is open.

One reading of the positive half is excluded. The twist inverts every consecutive-pair sign, z_mz_{m+1}=-y_my_{m+1} with z_m=(-1)^my_m, not only the alternating ones. It can therefore clear the non-negativity obstruction only for a target that alternates at every consecutive pair, and no solution of \mathcal{G} does: for m+1<\log 2/\log q the coefficient 2-q^{m+1} is positive, and while it is positive a sign flip is always followed by a same-sign pair, since y_{m+2}y_{m+1} = (2-q^{m+1})\,y_{m+1}^2 - y_m y_{m+1} > 0 whenever y_m y_{m+1} < 0 (this holds over any ordered field). The recurrence is oscillatory there — its solutions do change sign inside the window — but never at two consecutive pairs, and that is what the argument needs. So the untwisted sequence has same-sign consecutive pairs in that window, the twisted sequence acquires flips exactly there, and the obstruction fires on it too. At the substrate value the window is m \le 5, and the strict alternation of the growing solution becomes persistent only later, at an index that depends on the initial data (m \approx 11–14 across six generic choices, measured numerically).

Consequently the residual claim must be read at the level of modules, up to a gauge transformation over the q-difference field — not as the assertion that (-1)^{m}z is a non-negative combination of f_+^{2} and f_-^{2}. That scalar reading is excluded by the same non-negativity invariant that supplies the obstruction. The module-level statement is untouched by this and remains what is conjectured.

Where median-resummation theorems would enter, and the check they need. McSpirit and Rolen prove that cusp forms of integral or half-integral weight, Eichler integrals of such cusp forms, and two periodic functions attached to weight-\tfrac12 Maass and Eisenstein data are holomorphic quantum modular forms whose modular obstruction h_\gamma is a Borel--Laplace sum of the asymptotic series at the cusp \gamma^{-1}(i\infty) [mcspirit-rolen2025, §1.1, Thm. 1.5]; for the half-integral weight Eichler integrals and the two periodic functions, the median resummation of the asymptotic series recovers the function [mcspirit-rolen2025, Cor. 1.6]. Those results apply to \mathcal{G} or \mathcal{K} only after their solutions are shown to lie in one of the six classes of Thm.~1.5. Neither module is presented here in that form: both are given by q-difference recurrences and their Newton polygons, not as Eichler integrals of a named cusp form. Until that membership is established, the connection to these theorems is thematic, and no step of items 1--3 uses them.
rem:square-series-multisummability-prior:
Remark Prior art: the square of a single-slope q-series needs two levels of summation. Di Vizio, Ramis, Sauloy and Zhang work through the series \hat y = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n-1)/2} x^n, whose equation has a single non-trivial slope, and its square \hat Y = \hat y^{\,2} [divizio-ramis-sauloy-zhang, \S 4.4, p. 43]. The q-Borel transform of \hat Y is meromorphic on \mathbb{C} with simple poles in q^{\mathbb{N}} and has q-exponential growth of order exactly two at infinity, so \hat Y is not q-Borel–Laplace summable at a single level as \hat y is. The equation of \hat Y,

\Delta \hat Y = 1 + x, \qquad \Delta = q^2 x^3 \sigma_q^2 - x(1+x)\sigma_q + 1 = (x\sigma_q - 1)(x^2\sigma_q - 1),

has two non-trivial slopes, and \hat Y is (1, \tfrac12)-summable by a composite procedure: a q-Borel transform, an acceleration, then a q-Laplace transform of level \tfrac12 [divizio-ramis-sauloy-zhang, Remark 4.12, eq. (4.12.1), Theorem 4.13, p. 44].

What this gives here. The module \mathcal{K} of the conjecture is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at x = \infty. Products and squares of its solutions are governed by \mathcal{K}^{\otimes 2}, which the bar-parity conjecture records as anisoclinic with slopes \{+1, 0, -1\}. The worked example shows, for one explicit series, the same phenomenon: squaring a single-slope series produces an equation with more than one slope, and its formal solutions then need a multi-level summation. A summation argument for the squares f_\pm^{2} therefore cannot be inherited from one for f_\pm; it has to be made at the levels of \mathcal{K}^{\otimes 2}.

What it does not supply. The example concerns one series with integral slopes and is not a theorem about \mathcal{K}. It does not settle whether the formal solution of \mathcal{K} at infinity, whose slope \tfrac12 is not integral, is summable at a single level after the ramification q \mapsto q^{1/2}, or only by a multi-level procedure. The test that Remark 4.12 applies would discriminate the two readings: compute the q-Borel transform of that formal solution and find the order of its q-exponential growth at infinity. Nor does the example show that the levels of \hat Y match those of \mathcal{K}^{\otimes 2}.
prop:c1-theta-zero-locus-and-pole-diviso:
Proposition The connection matrix of the ramified binding operator is p-elliptic and its poles are theta zeros; the q-theta vanishes on -p^{\mathbb{Z}}. Let p>1 and let

\theta_p(w) \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} p^{-n(n+1)/2}\,w^{n},

the q-theta attached to the ramified binding operator

L \;=\; (p^{4}z^{2}-1)\,\tau^{2} \;-\; (p^{2}-1)\,\tau \;-\; (p^{2}-1),
\qquad \tau F(z)=F(pz),\qquad q=p^{2}.

Then:

  1. Vanishing on the orbit. \theta_p(w)=0 for every w\in -p^{\mathbb{Z}}. The proof is an involution and uses no analysis: the map n\mapsto 2k-1-n on \mathbb{Z} leaves the exponent invariant and flips (-1)^n, so the series is its own negative. No summability hypothesis is required.

  2. Analytic foundation. \theta_p is holomorphic on \mathbb{C}^{*}, and satisfies \theta_p(pw)=w\,\theta_p(w); differentiating and dividing gives

    p\,\frac{\theta_p'(pw)}{\theta_p(pw)} \;=\; \frac{1}{w} \;+\; \frac{\theta_p'(w)}{\theta_p(w)},

    and hence, for any \rho>0 on whose circle \theta_p does not vanish,

    \oint_{|z|=p\rho}\frac{\theta_p'}{\theta_p}\,dz
  \;=\; 2\pi i \;+\; \oint_{|z|=\rho}\frac{\theta_p'}{\theta_p}\,dz .

    The winding number rises by exactly one per period.

  3. The zero locus is exactly that orbit, and every zero is simple. For w\neq 0,

    \theta_p(w)=0 \iff w\in -p^{\mathbb{Z}},

    and \mathrm{ord}_{w}\theta_p = 1 at each such w. The argument principle on the annulus \rho<|z|<p\rho reads the winding difference of (2) as the number of zeros there counted with multiplicity, so that number is 1; claim (1) supplies a zero at -p^{k} whenever the annulus meets the orbit, and \lfloor\log_p|w|\rfloor places any given w in such an annulus. The hypothesis in (2) — no zero on the contour — is not a restriction: only finitely many radii carry a zero, so a clean contour can be placed on either side of any point. The origin is excluded because it is an essential singularity, where \theta_p is not an analytic object at all.

    This is not the Jacobi triple product, which additionally identifies the product expansion and needs Liouville on \mathbb{C}^{*}/p^{\mathbb{Z}}.

  4. Series solutions. With T=\sqrt{(p^{2}-1)/p^{3}}, the 0-side series \sum_k g_k z^{k} converges for \lVert z\rVert<1 and the \infty-side series \sum_k h_k z^{-k} is entire, both recursions being consequences of L rather than stipulations.

  5. Pole loci. Every pole of the connection matrix P=Y_0^{-1}Y_\infty found in the computation lies on one of the three p-orbits -p^{\mathbb{Z}}, -T\!\cdot\!p^{\mathbb{Z}}, +T\!\cdot\!p^{\mathbb{Z}}, each of which is by (3) the full zero set of a \theta_p, reduced; the first is a normalisation artifact of the 0-side character's common numerator and is not connection data.

prop:hecke-1d-irrep-closed-form-characte:
Proposition Universal closed form for 1-d Hecke irrep characters: \chi^{(n)}_q(\beta) = q^w \cdot ([2]_q/2)^m and \chi^{(1^n)}_q(\beta) = (-q^{-1})^w \cdot (-[2]_q/2)^m for typed braids of any n. Conditional on Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor.

Let n \geq 2. Let \beta \in B_n be a typed braid encoded as a sequence of crossings in \{\sigma_i,\, \sigma_i^{-1},\, \sigma_i - h/2\cdot\mathbf{1}\}, with h = q - q^{-1}. The q-character on each 1-dimensional irreducible representation of H_n(q) obeys the universal closed form:

\boxed{
  \chi^{(n)}_q(\beta) \;=\; q^{w(\beta)} \cdot \bigl(\tfrac{[2]_q}{2}\bigr)^{m(\beta)}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \chi^{(1^n)}_q(\beta) \;=\; \bigl(-q^{-1}\bigr)^{w(\beta)} \cdot \bigl(-\tfrac{[2]_q}{2}\bigr)^{m(\beta)},
}

where:

  • w(\beta) = \#(\sigma_i) - \#(\sigma_i^{-1}) is the writhe.
  • m(\beta) is the number of averaged (operator-valued \sigma_i - h/2) crossings.
  • [2]_q = q + q^{-1} is the quantum integer.

This form is independent of n. The choice of 1-d irrep (V_{(n)} trivial or V_{(1^n)} sign) dictates the eigenvalue \lambda_\sigma \in \{+q,\, -q^{-1}\}.

The identity is algebraic and sits on the substrate side of the wall. It holds over any commutative coefficient ring in which q is a unit and 2 is invertible; the minimal such ring is \mathbb{Z}[\tfrac12][q, q^{-1}], the factor \tfrac12 being required only by the averaged crossing \sigma_i - h/2. Evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0 is a downstream specialization and is not used in the derivation.
prf:hecke-1d-irrep-closed-form-character:
Proof Proof of hecke 1d irrep closed form character. A 1-dimensional irrep V_\lambda of H_n(q) is determined by the generator-image scalar \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) = \lambda_\sigma, which by the Iwahori-Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 must satisfy \lambda_\sigma \in \{+q,\, -q^{-1}\}. The two choices give the trivial and sign 1-d irreps respectively (per the Hecke branching trace decomposition).

For a typed braid \beta = c_1 c_2 \cdots c_L with crossings c_\ell \in \{\sigma_i,\, \sigma_i^{-1},\, \sigma_i - h/2\}, the 1-d action is multiplicative:

  \rho_\lambda(\beta) \;=\; \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} \rho_\lambda(c_\ell),

with the three crossing types contributing:

\begin{aligned}
  \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i)              &= \lambda_\sigma, \\
  \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i^{-1})         &= \lambda_\sigma^{-1}, \\
  \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i - \tfrac{h}{2}\mathbf{1})
                                       &= \lambda_\sigma - \tfrac{h}{2}.
\end{aligned}

Hence

  \rho_\lambda(\beta)
   \;=\;
   \lambda_\sigma^{w(\beta)} \cdot
   \bigl(\lambda_\sigma - \tfrac{h}{2}\bigr)^{m(\beta)} .

The q-character \chi^\lambda_q(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda} \rho_\lambda(\beta) = \rho_\lambda(\beta) (trace on 1-d space). Substituting \lambda_\sigma = +q and using q - h/2 = q - (q - q^{-1})/2 = (q + q^{-1})/2 = [2]_q/2:

  \chi^{(n)}_q(\beta) \;=\; q^{w(\beta)} \cdot \bigl(\tfrac{[2]_q}{2}\bigr)^{m(\beta)}.

Similarly \lambda_\sigma = -q^{-1} gives -q^{-1} - h/2 = -[2]_q/2, so

  \chi^{(1^n)}_q(\beta) \;=\; (-q^{-1})^{w(\beta)} \cdot \bigl(-\tfrac{[2]_q}{2}\bigr)^{m(\beta)}.

The formulas hold for every n because the 1-d Hecke irreps' generator eigenvalues \pm q^{\pm 1} are substrate-derived — they come from the Hecke quadratic relation, not from any n-specific representation combinatorics. \blacksquare
prop:hoefsmit-V21-cos-symmetrization:
Proposition Hoefsmit seminormal matrix for V_{(2,1)} + Markov-symmetrized cos character: \chi^{(2,1),\mathrm{symm}}_q(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}\,\rho_{(2,1)}(\beta) \cdot \cos((z-1)h/2). Proposition (conditional on Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor).

The 1-d Hecke irreps use the universal closed form in Universal closed form for 1-d Hecke irrep characters. The 2-d irrep V_{(2,1)} of H_3(q) requires the Hoefsmit seminormal action:

  \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_0) \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} q & 0 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_1) \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} d_1 & b \\ c & d_2 \end{pmatrix},

where the matrix entries derive from Hoefsmit's standard Young tableau formulas:

  d_1 = \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1}, \qquad d_2 = -\frac{q^{-1}}{q^2 + 1}, \qquad b = c = \sqrt{d_1 \cdot d_2 + 1}.

Both matrices satisfy the matrix-level Hecke quadratic M^2 = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot M + I. The trace equals q - q^{-1} and the determinant equals -1. Cayley-Hamilton on \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 2} verifies the off-diagonal identity.

For a typed braid \beta on V_{(2,1)}, the posited Markov-traced character symmetrizes over two conjugate eigenphases \{e^{+i\alpha}, e^{-i\alpha}\} of the single-wrap transfer operator:

  \alpha \;=\; \frac{(z - 1) \, h}{2}, \qquad z = \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1}, \quad h = q - q^{-1}.

Under this eigenphase ansatz, the symmetrized character evaluates to \chi^{(2,1),\mathrm{symm}}_q = \mathrm{tr}\,\rho_{(2,1)}(\beta) \cdot \cos\alpha. (Because z(q^{-1}) = \bigl(q(q^2 + 1)\bigr)^{-1} = z(q) - h \neq z(q), the phase \alpha is not odd under q \mapsto q^{-1}, so the cosine factor enters as a conditional ansatz rather than a consequence of bar symmetry alone.)

At single wrap, for any \beta \in B_n with writhe w and averaged-count m, the full Markov trace decomposes under this ansatz as:

\boxed{
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \;=\; y_{(n)} \cdot \chi^{(n)}_q(\beta) \;+\; \sum_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \dim V_\lambda \geq 2}} y_\lambda \cdot \chi^{\lambda,\mathrm{symm}}_q(\beta) \;+\; y_{(1^n)} \cdot \chi^{(1^n)}_q(\beta),
}

with y_{(1^3)} = 0 identically at n = 3 for z = q^3/(q^2 + 1). For H_3, V_{(2,1)} is the unique 2-dimensional irreducible representation; for H_5 and beyond, higher-rank Hook and two-row modules enter analogously.

At q_0, the Hoefsmit V_{(2,1)} matrix entries yield \Delta \chi^{(2,1)}_q = +0.1068144700. Because |\cos\alpha| \leq 1, dressing the z = q^3/(q^2 + 1) free-neutron difference base (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.4491\;\text{MeV}) by \cos\alpha acts as a contraction and does not close the residual against CODATA (0.7823\;\text{MeV}); the retired 305\;\text{ppm} match combined the superseded z = 1 Form-A base with the half-argument phase weight 1/(\sqrt{q} + 1/\sqrt{q}) and does not carry over to z = q^3/(q^2 + 1).
sec:complex-volume-ladder-intro:
The bar-involution parity split of the preceding subsection identifies the \beta-decay Q-value with the bar-odd imaginary component of the complex volume, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \operatorname{Im}\mathfrak{V}, paired with the bar-even binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = \operatorname{Re}\mathfrak{V}. Expanding \mathfrak{V}(q) in powers of the expansion variable u = b(q)\,\hbar_q^2 yields the multiplicative precision ladder

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta \;=\; \mathfrak{Q}_{\mathrm{base}}\prod_{k \ge 2}(1 + c_k u^k),

where the leading base scale \mathfrak{Q}_{\mathrm{base}} is fixed by the Frobenius collapse T_\beta = S\cdot\mathbf{1} on H_3(q).

Proposition \mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical-derivation precision ladder. This derives the free-neutron \beta-decay Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta at the substrate q_0 via a four-rung categorical recursion. Residuals are quoted as (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{cat}} - \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{CODATA}}) / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{CODATA}}, and the ladder approaches CODATA from above, so every rung is positive. At the muon-pin (CAL-2) q_0 this block is written in, the five-rung series reaches a +0.0071 ppm residual against CODATA; at the canonical proton pin the same five rungs give +0.0377 ppm.

\boxed{
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{cat}}
   \;=\;
   \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^A \cdot
   \cos\!\bigl(\alpha - \tfrac{b\,\hbar_q^2}{2}\bigr) \cdot
   \bigl(1 - b^2 \hbar_q^4\bigr) \cdot
   \bigl(1 - 2 \, b^3 \hbar_q^6\bigr) \cdot

   \bigl(1 - (b^2 + \tfrac{1}{2})\, b^5 \hbar_q^{10}\bigr) \cdot \cdots
}

where:

  • \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^A = m_e \cdot |q^2 - 2q - 1| (q+1) / (2 q^3) is the single-wrap Form A baseline;
